builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
summary: GraphBEAT replaces Transformer, LSTM, and standard GNN encoders for longitudinal EHR modeling with bucketized, temporally directed patient graphs using time-decay message passing and attention pooling. It is computationally cheap (over 250x fewer FLOPs, over 20x fewer parameters than sequence baselines) but requires multi-site longitudinal diagnosis and laboratory data plus clinical-domain validation. It can fail through site-specific documentation drift, leakage from incomplete records, and the lack of external or prospective clinical validation reported in the abstract.
rationale: This is a clinical EHR prediction method, not an inference-efficiency or LLM technique, so it is outside the reader's production adoption scope unless their product is healthcare risk stratification.
technique: Bucketized temporal graph learning for EHR risk prediction

claims.statement: GraphBEAT replaces Transformer, LSTM, and standard GNN encoders for longitudinal EHR modeling with bucketized, temporally directed patient graphs using time-decay message passing and attention pooling. It is computationally cheap (over 250x fewer FLOPs, over 20x fewer parameters than sequence baselines) but requires multi-site longitudinal diagnosis and laboratory data plus clinical-domain validation. It can fail through site-specific documentation drift, leakage from incomplete records, and the lack of external or prospective clinical validation reported in the abstract.

GraphBEAT requires over 250x fewer FLOPs per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than Transformer and LSTM baselines, while outperforming GNN and sequence-model baselines on cancer risk stratification at 12-, 24-, and 36-month lead times.
